Visual Design.assessment:
# Independent visual design review, first candidate

Baseline ran at port 4240 and the candidate at 4241. I opened both in a fresh Google Chrome session, with a 390×844 touch viewport and 900×900 and 1440×900 pointer viewports in light and pure-black themes. I compared the provided paired screenshots as well as separate live captures of Home, Blog, Azure Machine Configuration, Azure Documentation, Search results, Explorer navigation, the TOC, local and expanded global graphs, collapsed and expanded Mermaid, focus, hover and reduced motion. The supplied JWT and Linux-disk comparisons cover line-numbered code and table commands. No production files were edited.

## TX-02 — APPROVE

The additional half pixel helps distinguish punctuation, variable names and line numbers without drawing undue attention away from body copy. The Azure examples keep inline and fenced TX-02 aligned at 14.5px. The number gutter now tracks the code face, the syntax ink is legible in both themes and the existing 22px line spacing still gives each line room. In a live 14/14.5/15 comparison at 390px, the first six variable descriptions had identical line counts at 14 and 14.5. At 15 the first definition, beginning with `$version`, took a second line. With browser default text doubled, inline code, fenced content and gutter reached 29px together with 44px block leading. One variable description gained a line compared to 28px. This is ordinary text wrapping. The viewport stayed contained. No material defect or correction. The implementation uses one rem token and inherited gutter type. Update the code size in the design system when accepted.

## Mermaid controls — REVISE

The new top strip leaves the entire diagram visible. In the settled phone UI two distinct 44px controls sit above the horizontal flow diagram. The settled arrow and copy symbols share a baseline, outlines are conspicuous in both themes, navigation to Expand opens the diagram and Escape dismisses it. On hover-capable desktop the resting row retains Copy and the outline reveals Expand at keyboard focus. The strip costs approximately 52px of article height on touch and 40px on the desktop. The top-right VM label previously sat behind Copy and can now be read.

One material startup regression remains. The first candidate's provided 390px light Mermaid screenshot shows a single arrow where the paired controls should be. The independent screenshot with Mermaid's CDN module held demonstrated why. Copy starts at x322.45 and Expand at x316.45. Both are 44px wide, so Expand covers 38px of Copy. This persists until Quartz completes its asynchronous initialization, then Expand moves to x273.66. Eight normal loads also reproduced the incorrect initial geometry. The accepted build's invisible Expand does not paint over Copy during that interval. Use the known button width for the initial offset or hold Expand until Quartz attaches the handler and sets its offset. Retest with a held CDN response and after normal initialization. A denser toolbar or a different glyph is a preference, not a defect.

## Ten audit areas

| Area | Visual disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Component inventory | Keep shared treatments for Home, article, Blog, code, table, diagram, Explorer, TOC and Search. Each has a distinct visual role. |
| Editorial references and global layout | Keep the single reading column, common left edge and plain margins. Reference material supports a constrained, text-led reading page. The supplied OpenAI browser captures show a challenge page, so they cannot support claims about rendered OpenAI fonts. |
| Typography and article readability | Accept 14.5px TX-02 and the scaled gutter. Keep the Source Serif 4 hierarchy and the SN Pro UI. Heading sizes measured 30.20/42.26/43.52px across these Azure samples and their shared left edges were stable. |
| Archive hierarchy | Keep compact stacked phone metadata and the wider multi-column rows. Headlines retain priority in both themes. No defect from this pair of changes. |
| Light surfaces | Keep the warm #faf9f5 page, quiet panels and solid secondary ink. The technical surface separates a code example or diagram from surrounding prose. Correct the startup toolbar overlap. |
| Pure-black surfaces | Keep #000000 and the subtle secondary panels. The keyboard outline is visible against black. The diagram uses the existing palette. |
| Graphs and tables | Keep graph colors. Both wider sizes rendered local and global canvas; mobile and reduced motion suppressed them. Keep the table's scrolling cue. The phone command table is intentionally wider than the viewport and stays inside its scroll region. |
| Responsive and zoom | Keep current breakpoints, constrained measure and touch target proportions. At a doubled default the shared code size scales correctly. See the separate responsive reviewer for full browser zoom coverage. |
| Architecture and motion | Keep settled margins static. The warm or black space separates text, navigation and TOC. Added decorative geometry competes with the reading column. Reduced motion produced zero graph canvases and zero document animations after settling on Home. Preserve the existing Quartz interaction and remedy the initial Expand state locally. |
| Integrated audit | Accept the code update independently; return the Mermaid state for one correction. The article header, mobile navigation, search and archive were visually stable. Browser captures and geometry from the review are stored in this directory. |

Evidence includes `walk.cjs`, `4240.json`, `4241.json`, `surround-{390,900,1440}-{light,dark}.jpg`, `pair-{390,900,1440}-{light,dark}.jpg`, `type.json`, `startup-{accepted,first}.png` and `startup.log`. Native Safari and physical-device viewing were outside this individual Chrome review.

A responsive frame change also produced two superimposed Copy buttons at the same coordinates on both previews. This pre-existing Quartz behavior can create an extra keyboard stop and warrants separate investigation; the candidate did not introduce it.

# Revised build — independent visual design review

**TX-02 — APPROVE.** Reviewed the supplied baseline and revised Azure variable definitions, numbered JWT example and Linux command table at 390, 900 and 1440px in light and black. The 14.5px face gives identifiers and code digits slightly larger shapes while preserving the six sampled default phone definition heights. The shared unit and inherited gutter keep code and line numbers aligned. The numbered block measures the same 214px on the phone and 202px at both wider sizes in both builds. The earlier independent 14/14.5/15 comparison and doubled-default study still apply. The revision touched the Mermaid control.

**Mermaid — APPROVE.** I exercised the revised preview in twelve independent Chrome cases, delaying and failing the Mermaid CDN import in each of the six width/theme combinations. With the request outstanding or failed, the diagram source remained readable, Copy had a clear target and the clipboard contained the source. The inactive Expand control was hidden and could not take focus on failure. After releasing the request, the toolbar exposed two 44px touch controls on the phone. At normal text size their horizontal gap measured 4.80px and the diagram began 11px below the controls at every tested width. Focused Expand showed a 2px outline in both themes, Enter opened the diagram, and Escape closed it. Reduced motion gave the control a 0s transition. After doubling the browser text preference on an already-loaded page, the gap increased to 9.59px and diagram clearance to 23px in all six cases. Copy still received the center-point hit. The top-right VM label stays clear. The former 38px initial overlap is resolved. I found no material visual defect in the revision. The readiness selector depends on the current Quartz plugin's inline positioning hook, so the delayed and failed-load cases are worth repeating when that dependency is upgraded.

**Surrounding pages and integrated decision — APPROVE.** Compared new Chrome captures of Home, Blog, article and TOC, Azure search, mobile Explorer and the global graph with the baseline across all six configurations. Compact and wide archive rows retain their hierarchy. Warm and black page surfaces, flat margins, article alignment, restrained technical panels, graph palette and keyboard search outlines retain the intended appearance. Both larger frames rendered the local and expanded global graph. Keyboard dismissal restored graph-trigger focus. With reduced motion Home recorded zero canvases and zero document animations. The article and list did not acquire horizontal document scrolling. Both changes meet this review's visual gate.

I recommend adopting both changes and retaining the established component inventory, editorial layout, article hierarchy, archive rows, light and black palettes, graph and table treatments, responsive frame, and static margins. The initial report records individual findings for those ten audit areas. This individual review used desktop Linux Chrome and its emulated touch viewport.

Independent evidence includes `r2.json` for the 12 failure/delay states, `text-recheck.log` for doubled preferences, `4242.json` for page samples, `r2-graph.log` for the global graph, `r2-surround-*.jpg` for paired surrounding pages, and `final-pair-*.jpg` for the toolbar and technical examples. The first review and startup images remain beside this report.

Responsive and Accessibility.assessment:
# Independent responsive and accessibility assessment, first candidate

Compared the accepted preview on port 4240 with the candidate on port 4241. The live sample included Home, Blog, the Azure Machine Configuration article, the JWT numbered example, the Linux disk command table and the first diagram in the Microsoft Azure Documentation article. Inspected paired code, numbered fence, table, diagram and keyboard-focus screenshots at 390, 900 and 1440 pixels in light and pure-black dark themes. Chrome tested touch emulation, keyboard, interaction focus, forced colors, normal motion and reduced motion. Firefox 159 tested 100%, 200% and 400% native page zoom, including 400% with a browser-enforced 24px minimum font. An independent test glyph confirmed that font minimum took effect on the rendered advance.

## TX-02 code and gutter — APPROVE

- Bold article code, ordinary fenced code, line tokens and the line-number pseudo-element all use the 14.5px token. The 22px fenced leading persists. The 390px JWT panel reserves its gutter and scrolls locally via keyboard to the end. One sample's range grew from 27px to 39px while its document continued to fit the viewport.
- The phone Linux table keeps its keyboard focus ring, scrolls on ArrowRight and reaches the last column. In Firefox, the table reached its end at 400% page zoom with a 24px minimum. There was no document overflow on any of the four Firefox routes in the forty observations. Browser zoom narrowed the content viewport to 357 CSS pixels.
- Inline code retained 14.73:1 light and 13.88:1 dark text contrast. The visibly larger type and matching gutter do not change the hierarchy, the code color roles or the scrollbar semantics. One shared relative size and inherited counters avoid competing font sizes. No critical or material defect in the change.

## Mermaid Expand and protected diagram header — REVISE

- Touch receives a 44 × 44px visible Expand target beside the identically sized Copy target. At 900 and 1440 pixels the target measures 32 × 32px with a fine pointer. Tab reaches the actual Expand button, the final focus state is fully opaque, Enter opens the diagram and Escape closes it. Forced colors preserve a 2px ring and a visible system-colored icon. In light and black themes the resting icon contrast is 6.26:1 and 9.14:1. The focused desktop ring is 6.31:1 and 12.36:1 against the button surface.
- The candidate clears the SVG by 11px on all six browser/theme combinations. Baseline controls extended into the SVG by 41px on touch and 29px at the wider widths. The reading width and diagram aspect ratio are retained. Firefox also retained clearance at 400% zoom and with the 24px font minimum.
- Revision required, minor severity. With reduced motion enabled, newly focusing Expand runs a 200ms opacity transition. The ring and icon start at opacity 0. They reach 0.07 at 19ms, 0.41 at 53ms and 1 at 203ms. Quartz's more specific runtime transition declaration survives the universal reduced-motion reset. Scope the reduced-motion correction to Expand or the shared diagram controls and retest the first animation frame.
- Inherited, moderate accessibility issue. The Quartz expanded dialog leaves focus on the page's Expand button. Pressing Tab then reaches Copy behind the overlay. When Escape closes it, focus stays on Copy. This is identical on both previews. The trigger improvement does not introduce this behavior. The observations support an independent dialog focus-management correction.
- Inherited, lower severity. While the document stays loaded, changing the browser's standard font from 16px to 32px causes Expand and Copy to overlap. The plugin uses a one-time pixel measurement of Copy. Overlap is 24.8px in baseline and 22.4px in the candidate. With a browser default of 32px at load, the candidate leaves a 9.6px gap. A CSS offset derived from the current Copy-size token can avoid retaining the obsolete pixel measurement.
- The Home skip link and mobile Explorer keyboard dismissal, Blog search results and their 2px active-option ring, and return focus to Search all worked. Tablet and desktop global graph opened and returned focus to its trigger on dismissal. Reduced motion suppressed the graph.

Evidence files in this directory include the paired screenshot contact sheets, independent viewport observations, dedicated diagram keyboard and touch observations in each theme, forced-colors measurements, Firefox zoom and minimum-font samples, and frame-by-frame reduced-motion measurements. The first broad interaction trace contained transient theme initialization and an adjacent-diagram focus observation on one mobile run. Dedicated diagram and code checks pinned the theme before navigation, verified the focused button's identity and waited for the actual dialog state.

# Independent responsive and accessibility assessment, corrected candidate

Compared the generated site on port 4242 to the accepted site on 4240, and reproduced the two previous interaction failures on port 4241 before retesting the correction. Inspected paired captures at 390, 900 and 1440 pixels in light and pure-black dark modes, including code, numbered fences, tables, Mermaid drawings and startup states. The live pages were Home, Blog, the Azure Machine Configuration article, the JWT example, the Linux disk table and the Microsoft Azure Documentation diagram.

## TX-02 inline, fenced and line-number sizing — APPROVE

- Article code, fenced commands and numbered lines share the 14.5px token, and fenced lines retain 22px leading. The TX-02 family, normal and bold treatment, syntax colors and light/dark contrast remain intact. Keyboard scrolling in the narrow JWT example reaches the final column over a 39px range. The Linux command table accepts keyboard scrolling and keeps focus visible.
- Fresh Firefox 159 samples covered four pages at 100%, 200% and 400% actual page zoom, including a real minimum font size of 24px. The document stayed within the available width in all 20 observations, and internal scroll containers remained usable. A separate eight-observation reflow check at exactly 320 CSS pixels passed with and without the 24px minimum on all four pages. At a 357px client width, Firefox reached the last table column after 609px of local scrolling with the minimum enabled.
- A common relative size and inherited gutter type keep future sizing changes together. No demonstrated regression in typography, reflow, clipping or access.

## Mermaid control and protected diagram header — APPROVE

- At reduced motion the corrected Expand indicator is fully opaque on the focus event and every subsequent sampled animation frame. Computed transition duration is 0s. On the prior candidate, the same keyboard action exposed the 200ms fade.
- Changing the browser's default font from 16px to 32px while the same document is open leaves 9.59px between the two 64px controls, matching a fresh load with the larger setting. The previous candidate overlapped them by 22.41px. The narrow selector and documented CSS override address the plugin's one-time inline pixel offset.
- With the Mermaid module delayed or permanently blocked, source text stayed readable, the Copy button received pointer hits, Enter copied the expected source, and the dormant Expand control could receive neither programmatic nor keyboard focus. All three viewport widths passed. Releasing the delayed module added a usable Expand button. Shift+Tab from Copy reached the correct button, then Enter opened its diagram.
- With the module loaded, touch exposes a 44px target, and fine-pointer keyboard access has a 32px target and a 2px focus ring. The two controls clear the drawing by 11px. Their system-colored icons and outline are visible in forced colors. Enter and touch open the drawing, Escape closes it. The surrounding articles, 56-entry Blog list, search result selection, Escape focus return, mobile Explorer and tablet/desktop graph interaction retained their earlier behavior. Reduced motion suppressed the graph.
- One inherited accessibility issue remains. The Quartz dialog keeps focus on its trigger when it opens. Tabbing reaches the background Copy control, where focus remains if Escape then closes the overlay. This is identical on the accepted baseline and both candidates. It is a moderate upstream interaction issue beyond the changed trigger styling.

Frame samples, live font resizing, delayed and blocked module probes, forced-color data, the Firefox runs, and the six browser viewport/theme records are available in the corrected evidence directory. The paired contact sheets include the original baseline and the two candidate startup comparisons.

CSS and Quartz V5.assessment:
# CSS and Quartz V5 review J, first candidate

## Editorial code typography — APPROVE

Chrome compared the frozen and candidate pages at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 under both light and pure-black dark modes. I inspected all six supplied pairs for inline, numbered, table, resting Mermaid and focused Mermaid states alongside my own browser captures. I traversed Home, the Blog folder, Azure Machine Configuration, Linux disk space, JWT and the Azure documentation. The search query “azure” supported arrow selection and Escape. I opened the mobile Explorer and the tablet global graph, used search with keyboard focus and checked graph suppression under reduced motion.

The existing rem token makes regular and bold TX-02 inline code 14.5px and retains weights 400 and 700. Numbered fences use the same 14.5px size and 22px line height. Their sticky gutter inherits that size. Syntax and gutter colors, Source Serif 4 paragraph metrics, gutters and graph inks match the previews. On the 390px disk-space article, the wider command table scrolls in its 355px wrapper. The document stays 390px wide. On desktop the table fits. Baseline versus candidate differ by a few characters in some wraps, with no clipping or escaped page width. No material defect. The explicit 14px design-system entry needs its normal documentation update if accepted.

## Mermaid controls — REVISE

The candidate reuses the existing button classes, ink, target-size token and inset focus treatment within Markdown pre blocks. It preserves the plugin's inline computed right offset after initialization. The ready diagram has a full header row before its SVG with enough clearance to read its upper-right VM label. On touch both controls are visibly distinct, 44px square, with a 4.8px horizontal gap. The keyboard focus outline is 2px. Enter opened the diagram dialog and Escape closed it in both themes at all three sizes. The source changes are limited to the existing stylesheet and introduce no new JavaScript.

1. **Material, dependency failure and delayed startup.** With the cdnjs Mermaid request blocked, the new Expand is 44px square, sits 6px left of Copy and covers about 38px of Copy's 44px width. A hit test at Copy's center returns Expand. Keyboard Enter on Expand does nothing. The frozen baseline still lets a pointer hit Copy at its center. The active Obsidian Flavored Markdown 1.0.0 plugin inserts Expand into built HTML and installs the listener and its inline position only after rendering. The syntax-highlighting 1.0.1 plugin initializes Copy separately. Hide Expand (including focus and hit testing) until ready, preserving Copy during failure. An inline right style set by the plugin explicitly signals initialization. Keep separation between controls and the drawing or fallback source.
2. **Minor, reduced motion.** With prefers-reduced-motion set to reduce, the computed transition is still 0.2s. A focused Expand fades in from 0 on the fine-pointer layout. At the second animation frame the opacity was ~0.07 at 900px, and Chrome reported active opacity and outline transitions. Touch also animates the outline. The Mermaid plugin injects its own button transition, including on pre:hover. Suppress the transition within this scoped button rule under reduced motion and test actual focus and hover (including a hovered pre). The fade on newly revealed focus is specific to this candidate.

Inspection used the actual dependency's packaged scripts and generated DOM, the supplied screenshot pairs under /tmp/quartz-pub/pairs-{4240,4241}, my own per-viewport JSON, source/failure captures and contact sheets in this directory. The two decisions are independent. The Mermaid revision needs another assessment after rebuilding.

# CSS and Quartz V5 review J, revised candidate

## Code typography — APPROVE

I repeated the browser traversal on the rebuilt preview at 390 × 844, 900 × 900 and 1440 × 900 in light and pure-black dark modes and compared it with the frozen baseline and first candidate. I inspected the supplied image pairs and my own Home, Blog listing, Azure article, Linux command table, JWT and Azure diagram states. Search arrow selection, mobile Explorer, tablet global graph and the reduced-motion layouts behaved as in the earlier review.

TX-02 regular and bold inline code are 14.5px at 400/700 weight. The block and its line-number pseudo-element both compute to 14.5px/22px. Source Serif paragraph metrics and syntax/gutter colors match the first candidate. No clipping, page overflow or unintended selector spillover appeared. The usual scrollable phone table contains the wider commands. Some supplied numbered-code screenshots caught the page before Copy initialized, including 390px light. My repeat, waiting for the actual control, shows Copy in both themes at all widths. The implementation has no demonstrated regression here. Record the 14.5px token in the accepted design system.

## Mermaid controls — APPROVE

The scoped selector applies only to a direct Expand button on a Markdown pre with Mermaid code. The current Obsidian Flavored Markdown plugin sets its inline right declaration synchronously in the same loop iteration in which it binds Expand. Before this signal, visibility:hidden removes the unready affordance from hit testing and focus while retaining space for the source and Copy. With the CDN held, clicking the center of Copy placed the complete Mermaid source (the plugin normalizes the final newline) on the browser clipboard at every size and in both themes. Blocking the CDN indefinitely left Copy reachable. After releasing the same request, both targets worked. Enter opened the graph dialog, Escape closed it, and reopening after a live theme switch worked in all six cases. The touch target was 44px square. The controls cleared the SVG by 11px at the default size.

The one !important declaration overrides the plugin's one-time inline pixel offset. The scope and source comment explain the dependency. On a 1440px page I changed Chrome's default font size live from 16 to 24 to 32 and back to 16. After layout settled, the first candidate overlapped the controls by 8.81px at 24 and 22.41px at 32. The revision maintained positive gaps of 4.80, 7.19, 9.59 and 4.80px respectively. The explicit reduced-motion rule also wins over the later runtime stylesheet's pre:hover declaration. Focus and hover yielded immediate opacity 1, 0s transition and no active Expand animations. No material defect remains in either proposal.

**Minor inherited behavior.** Copy still uses the plugin's 200ms transition in all three builds. When Chrome's default text size is abruptly halved, its former width can briefly consume part of the gap while it shrinks. This does not affect the settled positions or the corrected reduced-motion reveal on Expand. The current plugin exposes readiness through its inline right style, so an upstream change to that contract warrants repeating the startup check.

**Evidence.** The per-viewport metrics, live clipboard and theme-switch records, settled resizing comparison and browser captures are in this directory. The paired startup sheets show the pending fallback on the first and revised candidates. The supplied pairs and the settled phone capture establish the difference between a pre-initialization screenshot and normal numbered code. See clipboard-4242-*.json, settled-{4240,4241,4242}.json, metrics-4242-*.json, 4242-390-light-blocked.json and 4242-*-number.jpg.

Design Director.assessment:
# Design Director · preimplementation decisions

I opened the accepted production-build preview on port 4240 in Google Chrome. I inspected Home, Blog, Azure Documentation and Azure Machine Configuration at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in light and black themes. The 390px context emulated a touch pointer. I compared 14, 14.5 and 15px in the actual article and studied the table/command comparison boards. The screenshots and measurements are in this directory, with type trials in ../type, source studies in ../anthropic and ../openai, and the component census in ../architecture.

- **Initial position, superseded by the follow-up below.** Approve an implementation trial of 0.9375rem for the shared TX-02 token. The owner wants larger technical type while preserving parity. The regular commands and bold identifiers gain clarity against surrounding prose at 15px. The unchanged 22px line-height token leaves a visible distinction between code lines. In the 390px Chrome trial, changing to 15px let the list's first explanation extend by one line. Command cells in the disk article gained around 1px per text line, while both tables kept their existing scroll widths. The 14.5px candidate showed less differentiation and its measured ten-line sample acquired a 23px pitch, compared with 22px at 14 and 15. Keep role, font weight, syntax ink and scrolling unchanged. Review 24px/32px preferences, local scrollability and focus on the rebuilt candidate.
- **Approve an implementation trial for the existing Mermaid Expand control.** At rest the control has opacity 0 on a 390px touch screen. The adjacent 44px Copy covers the upper-right VM box of the first Azure flowchart. Reserve a stable control row or equivalent protected area above the SVG. Support a visible resting control on touch and a visible keyboard focus state, match adjacent Copy geometry and test both controls wherever they appear. Pointer/keyboard state shifts must not move the diagram during interaction. Exercise all ten published diagrams and the expanded view. The pre-existing unlabeled dialog, absence of a keyboard-operable Close button and background Tab path require component semantics, beyond the visual change. Preserve the issue in the final inventory.
- **Reject paragraph text-wrap: pretty for this publication iteration.** Chromium removed single-word endings without extra lines in the 249 observations. WebKit lengthened ten paragraphs, and native Firefox retained the fallback. The trial’s exclusions for images, captions, hard breaks, signature and inline technical material add selector maintenance for an optional visual preference. Current prose measure and typographic rhythm support comfortable reading.
- **Retain existing prose/title families and measure, listing density, search, page canvas and graph.** The evidence supports preserving the separate roles of Source Serif 4, SN Pro and TX-02. The airier archive trial cost a full visible row at all three widths. Both source references support separating titles from metadata. Keep the high-contrast warm/black canvases and the present restrained interaction styling.

The decisions above preauthorize the two trials. Final acceptance requires the paired candidate screenshots, independent reviewer decisions and automated checks. Moderate service limitations and component accessibility gaps belong in the component inventory.


## Final preimplementation code-size decision

**Approve a shared 0.90625rem TX-02 token and inherited size on the sticky line numbers.** On closer comparison at 900px, two Disk command rows wrapped at 15px and an additional Azure fence required horizontal scrolling. The 14.5px sample retained the baseline scroll thresholds and table cadence. The tablet screenshot visibly shows the growpart placeholder moving onto a separate line at 15px. Both larger scales give the reader a wider glyph than the current 14px. Prior owner preferences and this evidence favor the intermediate size. Removing the line-number caption-size override restores a measured 22px line pitch in both engines for the intermediate trial. Verify the compiled cascade and declare inheritance explicitly only if needed. The revised decision supersedes the preliminary preference for 15px. The Mermaid, wrapping, and remaining retention decisions stand.

## Mermaid revision preapproval

Independent review caught a material interaction regression while the Mermaid import is pending or fails. The emitted Expand button exists before it is wired, is focusable, and covers Copy’s center in the initial candidate. The installed transformer awaits rendering, sets the inline right offset, then attaches the handler in one JavaScript task. Every published diagram includes the modal it queries between these statements. Approve a diagram-scoped visibility guard keyed to the inline right declaration, and check it during a delayed import, failure, recovery and ordinary success.

A no-reload browser-default change also leaves the plugin's measured pixel offset stale. Approve the one documented important right declaration matching the live control-size token, plus Copy's 0.375rem inset and a 0.3rem gap. Remove the earlier margin compensation. Suppress the plugin's hover/rest 200ms transition under the reader's reduced-motion preference. Test the keyboard path, Copy pointer target and both diagram controls after normal and enlarged-default resizing. Keep the pre-existing CSS-hidden Pixi lifecycle issue in the backlog. Resolving that requires changes to JavaScript mount eligibility and a separate scope review.

# Integrated gate · iteration 10

**APPROVE index-530afd62.css for both CSS changes.** H (visual design), I (responsive/accessibility) and J (CSS/Quartz V5) independently reviewed the correction and each approved both changes. Their reports are ../review-visual/assessment-final.md, ../review-access/corrected.md and ../review-css/review-revised.md. The initial candidate failed the control gate and was superseded.

I examined the frozen and corrected sites in distinct Chrome contexts at 390×844, 900×900 and 1440×900 in both themes. My live pages included the Azure Documentation diagram, Azure Machine Configuration definitions, the affected project command table, Blog and Home. The twelve state records are gate-{4240,4242}-{390,900,1440}-{light,dark}.json with paired diagram and identifier screenshots beside them. A browser run repeated search after waiting for the initialized combobox. I also inspected the three independent visual, keyboard, widget and dependency-failure studies and the graph and table audits.

- The inline identifier, fenced code and sticky line number all measured 14.5px and a numbered row measured 22px. The shared scale enlarges average character advances by 3.6%. Device-scale-one cap-height measurements rounded to the same value at 14 and 14.5. The 900px disk commands preserve the eight single-line rows and Azure fences keep four local scroll ranges at that width. Of all 23 published tables in each engine, only the first command reference table changed overflow eligibility, gaining 5px at 900px. I reached that edge; the full census records the keyboard region and fade clearing. The phone and desktop overflow counts remained 16 and 3. Keep this small tablet cost; globally compressing table cells or overriding the code scale would affect many more examples.
- At 390px the settled toolbar shows separate 44px targets above the complete drawing. The desktop hover/focus design remains quiet at rest. During the held import the dormant button had hidden visibility and would not accept focus, and Copy responded at its center. Releasing the import made the keyboard target available. In all six corrected contexts, focus showed a 2px outline with full opacity, reduced motion had a 0s transition, Enter opened the diagram and Escape dismissed it. Direct live root enlargement produced a settled 9.59px horizontal gap, compared with 4.80px at the default. The independent reviewers also exercised actual browser-default changes, the system color palette, clipboard, permanent dependency failure, theme change and 200%–400% Firefox page zoom. The corpus sweep covered ten published diagrams.
- Both site themes retain their reading surface. Search accepted an arrow-key selection across both builds, and reduced-motion Home had zero canvas elements. The other researchers recorded true graph node hover, zoom, navigation, escape/focus return, theme rebuild and tablet Home. In normal motion, the 900px ordinary article and desktop reader mode can run a CSS-hidden Pixi canvas. Suppressing that work needs a separate JavaScript lifecycle fix.
- The fully hydrated paired axe scans identify the same five IACS images without alternatives and the same four phone scroll regions on the CDN-blocked diagram article. My separate six-route/build controls confirmed valid desktop TOC target IDs after hydration and zero axe aria-valid-attr-value failures. The first automated pass caught some TOCs before the plugin had assigned their IDs. The existing Mermaid dialog focus/accessible naming, keyboard-inoperable collapsible callouts and responsive duplicate Copy targets warrant concrete component backlog entries. Native Safari, screen readers, physical-device input, field performance and the authored media's editorial meaning limit conclusions. Keep row-level inventory statuses qualified.
- A fresh Quartz V5 build emitted 913 files, all 164 unit tests passed, scoped formatting passed, and route/title/metadata/JavaScript/content-index integrity matched across 252 HTML outputs. The full check remains nonzero at the TypeScript stage on the two existing micromorph and remark-parse dependency errors. The repository workflow's build-and-test job runs only for the upstream repository. The compile errors remain visible as baseline limitations.

## Substantive evaluations 1–10

| Cycle | Supported decision |
| --- | --- |
| 1. Inventory | Adopt the generated route/selector/plugin census and mark absent or untested states separately. Record accessible naming and focus limitations. |
| 2. Editorial references | Retain the warm page, neutral structure and 43rem reading measure. The Chromium wrapping gain came with extra WebKit lines and complicated selectors. |
| 3. Typography | Choose 14.5px relative TX-02 with inherited gutter size. Retain serif prose and title with the current heading scale. |
| 4. Listings | Keep distinct mobile metadata and the existing desktop grid. More padding consumed one full visible item at each primary width. |
| 5. Light | Keep warm surfaces, solid secondary ink, existing dividers and syntax colors. The code and control comparisons preserved hierarchy and readability. |
| 6. Dark | Keep the black canvas, soft-white type, near-black code surface and existing syntax inks. Both controls have distinct readable shapes above the drawing. |

## Provisional rubric

Scores use the requested 0–10 scale and weights in order. Treat ratings as ordinal editorial assessments. On this scale, 9 means strong measured performance across tested use cases; 8 includes bounded implementation or integration limitations; 7 reflects a demonstrated user-facing or runtime gap even with strong primary flows. Half-steps express mixed findings within a category. A score cannot waive a functional or accessibility defect.

| Criterion | Weight | Corrected site | Basis |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Beauty and editorial character | 15% | 9 | Calm margins, stable measure and differentiated content/metadata hierarchy across both themes. |
| Typography and sustained reading | 15% | 9 | Three distinct type roles, normal and emphasized inline code parity, intact row pitch and usable enlarged text. |
| CSS consistency and maintainability | 15% | 8.5 | Existing token and owner rules; a single necessary, localized inline-style override relies on upstream readiness. |
| Light and black themes | 15% | 9 | Confirmed page colors, readable syntax, subdued UI rules and independently themed diagrams. |
| Responsive design | 10% | 9 | Three-width primary engagement, native Firefox zoom, an unobscured diagram and local overflow. |
| Quartz components and graph | 10% | 8 | Search, navigation and graph interactions pass; plugin dialog focus and hidden graph lifecycle remain. |
| Tables and technical content | 5% | 8.5 | Diagram labels survive and code/table scrolling works; one 5px tablet scroll and raw fallback are documented. |
| Accessibility and usability | 10% | 7 | Trigger access and reduced-motion focus improve. Confirmed outstanding author alternatives and plugin semantics preclude a higher assessment. |
| Motion and performance | 5% | 7.5 | Stationary reading page and immediate reduced motion. The hidden Pixi graph still schedules recurring work in normal motion. |

Weighted result **8.525/10**. The integrated design gate accepts the stylesheet. Three distinct post-minimum evaluations, documentation/inventory and the terminal independent audit still belong to the larger goal.
